rationale: Evidence: iteration 8 (kd 1.5) scored 534.3, the best so far. The oval finishes 20 of 20 runs at 1.94 s with rms 0.0097. The s-bend finishes 9 of 20 (progress 0.83), and the slalom still never finishes (progress 0.17, about 1 line-loss event per run, all off track). Each kd step has helped: kd 0.9 to 1.2 gave +69, and kd 1.2 to 1.5 gave +83. Max error sits at the off-track limit on the bends with low rms, which fits transient overshoot into bends. The change: kd 1.5 to 2.0, a continuation of the one lever that has worked. Geometry (5 sensors at x = -0.04 to 0.04, y = 0.06, 16 mm footprint, body 0.18 x 0.16 m, 0.8 kg, wheel track 0.12 m), kp 5.0, ki 4.0, base_speed 1.2 and last_direction line loss are held fixed so the kd effect reads cleanly against iteration 8. Expected result: s-bend finish rate and progress rise, slalom progress rises above 0.17, and the oval holds near 2 s. Risks: kd amplifies sensor noise and may increase steering_oscillation (currently about 0.2 on the oval, 0.35 on the s-bend). Hypotheses for next: (H1) kd 2.0 still improves the s-bend, so the next step is kd near 2.5. (H2) If the gain shrinks (diminishing returns), turn-in speed is the limit and base_speed should drop to about 1.1. (H3) Slalom line loss comes from fast direction changes at the 0.04 m array edge, so a 7-sensor array at plus or minus 0.045 m is the next geometry test. Measurements requested per track: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors and noise_robustness.
